solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Deadly spray a fellow used with fruit

parts.note: a gent is a gentleman, a fellow
an orange is a citrus fruit

explanation.surface: A sinister recipe: some man mixing a lethal spray with fruit.
explanation.definitionFit: Agent Orange was the toxic defoliant herbicide sprayed by US forces during the Vietnam War.

clue.text: Gather what's finally going spare

indicators.note: finally points to the closing letter of the word going

parts.note: spare and lean both mean thin, with no excess flesh

explanation.surface: Collecting whatever is left over and going spare.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spare' looks like 'surplus' in the surface, but here it means thin.
explanation.definitionFit: To glean is to gather bit by bit, as gleaners collect leftover grain after harvest.

clue.text: Old Poles in National Trust work continuously

indicators.note: in places the old poles within the trust's abbreviation

parts.note: NT is the abbreviation for the National Trust, the British heritage charity
N and S are the north and south poles
OP is short for opus, a musical work

explanation.surface: Elderly Polish workers labour without a break at a National Trust property.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Poles' suggests people from Poland; here it means the magnetic poles N and S. The National Trust looks after historic houses in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something nonstop means doing it without any pause or break, continuously.

clue.text: Manoeuvre around hint of rumour in death notice

indicators.note: in puts the hint of rumour within the short word for a death notice

parts.note: an obit is an obituary, a newspaper death notice

indicators.note: a hint of a word is just its opening letter, here of rumour

explanation.surface: A rumour hinted at in an obituary sets someone manoeuvring.
explanation.definitionFit: To orbit something is to travel in a circuit around it, as a satellite circles a planet.

clue.text: Helipad moving to Paris

indicators.note: moving suggests the letters of to Paris being shifted into a new order

explanation.surface: A helicopter landing pad is relocating to Paris.
explanation.walkthrough: 'moving' rearranges the letters of TO PARIS.
explanation.definitionFit: An airstop is a landing place for helicopters, essentially a heliport or helipad.

clue.text: Win something Gateshead, Galashiels, Dungannon, Donegal and Reigate all have

definitions.meaning: to win is to acquire or obtain something, a profit

definitions.text: something Gateshead, Galashiels, Dungannon, Donegal and Reigate all have
definitions.meaning: each of these place names has the letters G and A in it

explanation.surface: A prize shared by five towns of the British Isles.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the answer as two words, GA IN: every one of the five place names contains the letters GA. They are towns in England, Scotland, Northern Ireland and Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: Winning something and acquiring it are synonyms: a victory brings an advantage or profit.

clue.text: Pokes quietly with sticks

parts.note: P is piano, the musical direction for playing quietly
rods are sticks; with is a joining word read with them

explanation.surface: Someone gently jabs at something using sticks.
explanation.definitionFit: Prods and pokes are both jabs with a finger or pointed object.

clue.text: Means to control extremes of rage at home

indicators.note: extremes of picks the two end letters of the word rage

parts.note: in means at home, as in staying in

explanation.surface: How to keep one's temper in check at home.
explanation.definitionFit: A rein is a strap used to guide and restrain a horse, hence any means of control.

clue.text: German city-dweller to live right next to ship

parts.note: to be is to exist, to live
a liner is a large passenger ship

explanation.surface: A German urbanite settling down beside a moored ship.
explanation.definitionFit: A Berliner is an inhabitant of Berlin, Germany's capital.

clue.text: Establish unit: set it in motion

indicators.note: in motion says the letters of unit set it are stirred into a fresh order

explanation.surface: Instructions to found a unit and get it going.
explanation.definitionFit: To institute something is to set it up or found it, which is to establish it.

clue.text: Visibly embarrassed as books are spoken of

indicators.note: spoken of says the word for what books are is said out loud, giving its sound-alike

parts.note: books are read, in the past-tense pronunciation that rhymes with bed

explanation.surface: Someone blushing as their books are discussed.
explanation.definitionFit: Going red in the face is the visible sign of embarrassment, a blush.

clue.text: Manage to flee

definitions.meaning: to manage a business is to direct it
to flee is to escape at speed

explanation.definitionFit: Running a shop means managing it, and running away means fleeing.

clue.text: Is not prudent using paper at first: expecting litter!

indicators.note: at first takes the opening letter of each of the five words before it

explanation.surface: A disapproving remark about wasting paper, and then a surprise announcement about a litter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Litter' suggests rubbish, going with paper; it is a brood of puppies.
explanation.definitionFit: A bitch that is pregnant is said to be in pup, awaiting a litter of puppies.

clue.text: French marshal appearing periodically in Annecy

indicators.note: periodically takes every other letter of Annecy, the even ones

explanation.surface: A French military commander turns up from time to time in the Alpine town of Annecy.
explanation.definitionFit: Michel Ney was one of Napoleon's marshals, famous at Waterloo.

clue.text: Is salesman turning up on street last?

indicators.note: turning up in a down clue says the words Is and salesman are read upwards, backwards

parts.note: a rep is a sales representative

explanation.surface: Wondering whether a salesman arriving on the street is the final one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'last' looks like the adjective 'final'; it is the verb, to endure.
explanation.definitionFit: To persist is to continue to endure, so it means to last; the question mark flags the verb sense.

clue.text: Use train signal

definitions.meaning: use as a noun, the purpose: what's the use?
to train a gun is to aim it
to signal is to indicate with a finger

explanation.surface: An instruction to operate a railway signal.
explanation.walkthrough: Three definitions: 'train' looks like the railway, but it is the verb meaning aim.
explanation.definitionFit: There is no purpose in it, aim a weapon at, and indicate a direction: all three fit.

clue.text: Signs I'd since altered

indicators.note: altered tells us the letters of I'd since are changed around

explanation.surface: Someone notes that signs have changed since they last looked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'altered' rearranges the letters of I'D SINCE.
explanation.definitionFit: Indices are indicators or pointers, so signs of something, as in economic indicators.

clue.text: Fleet of foot, after short swim

indicators.note: after places foot following the cut-down word
short says the word swim is cut, losing its final letter

explanation.surface: Being quick on one's feet after a brief swim.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fleet of foot' reads as one phrase; the definition is only 'Fleet'.
explanation.definitionFit: Fleet as an adjective means fast, nimble and quick-moving.

clue.text: Sardonic and cautious, dismissing article

indicators.note: dismissing means sending away, so the article is taken out

explanation.surface: Someone is mocking and careful, sending away a newspaper piece.
explanation.definitionFit: Wry humour is dry and mocking, a close synonym of sardonic.

clue.text: People on a mission could be rude, crass

indicators.note: could be hints that rude crass might become other letters once rearranged

explanation.surface: Missionaries risk coming across as rude and crass.
explanation.definitionFit: Crusaders are campaigners pursuing a cause, people on a mission, originally the medieval holy warriors.

clue.text: Tease us for bringing up term of endearment

indicators.note: bringing up in a down clue says the letters are read upwards, in reverse

parts.note: to rag someone is to tease them

explanation.surface: Teasing us is meant as an affectionate pet name.
explanation.definitionFit: Sugar is used as an affectionate name, like honey or sweetheart.

clue.text: Author dreaded missing tips

indicators.note: missing tips drops the outside letters of dreaded, keeping the middle

explanation.surface: A writer's fears lose their sharp edges.
explanation.definitionFit: Charles Reade was a Victorian novelist, best known for The Cloister and the Hearth.

clue.text: Chief attraction featuring in scenic lough

indicators.note: featuring in says the word sits within the letters of scenic lough

explanation.surface: The highlight of a pretty Irish lake.
explanation.walkthrough: A lough is an Irish lake.
explanation.definitionFit: A clou, from French for nail, is the main point of interest or star feature.

clue.text: English novelist's description of one cricket team

definitions.meaning: Henry, author of Tom Jones; the 's stands for is, joining the two definitions
in a cricket match one side bats and the other fields

explanation.definitionFit: Henry Fielding wrote Tom Jones, and in cricket the side not batting is the fielding team.

clue.text: Fuel that's firm and pale in the middle

parts.note: CO is short for company, a firm

indicators.note: in the middle keeps only the central letters of pale

explanation.surface: A fuel described as solid and pale at its core.
explanation.walkthrough: 'firm' looks like an adjective (solid); it is a business.
explanation.definitionFit: Coal is a fossil fuel burned for heat and power.

clue.text: Address mute, deranged Shakespearean fairy

indicators.note: deranged means thrown out of order, so these letters get rearranged

explanation.surface: Speaking to a silent, unhinged fairy from Shakespeare.
explanation.definitionFit: Mustardseed is one of Titania's attendant fairies in A Midsummer Night's Dream.
